name: Beam
tagline: eBay's distributed knowledge-graph store, later renamed Akutan, built around one central log; archived 2019.
description: Beam was a distributed RDF-style knowledge graph store that eBay open-sourced in April 2019 and renamed Akutan that July, shortly before archiving the repository. Every change is appended to a single central log (Apache Kafka in production, an in-memory log for development), and 'view' servers backed by RocksDB replay it to build partitioned indexes, which gives transactional updates and consistent historical snapshots in exchange for a global cap on write rate (tens of thousands of changes per second). Queries use a SPARQL-like language with a limited inference engine. eBay ran a 20-server development cluster with about 2.5 billion facts, but the authors stated it was not ready for production-critical use, lacking fact deletion, backup/restore and automated cluster management.
statusNote: Renamed Akutan in July 2019 and the eBay GitHub repository was archived the same month; never production-ready.
basedOn: Apache Kafka log and RocksDB views

scale.notes: Reads and storage scale with view servers; all writes go through one log, capping total change rate. Tested with ~2.5 billion facts on 20 servers.

strengths: Simple log-centric architecture that yields transactions and global snapshots
Historical queries against any past log position
Read capacity scales by adding view servers
Well-documented design notes from eBay engineers
weaknesses: Global write throughput is limited by the single log
Missing fact deletion, backup/restore and cluster automation
Query language is close to, but not compatible with, SPARQL
useCases: Studying log-structured distributed graph store designs
